title: Removal of a Wing Tank Access Panel and Preparation for Tank Entry

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of a wing tank access panel and preparation of the tank for entry, covering defuelling, purging, atmosphere monitoring and the panel seal land inspection that governs the closure.

sections.purpose: This task removes a wing tank access panel and prepares the tank for entry, and records the seal land condition that determines how the panel is to be closed.
sections.job_setup_note: Tank entry is a confined space operation. The tank must be defuelled, drained, purged and continuously monitored, and an attendant must remain at the aperture for the whole time a person is inside. Do not remove more than the number of panels given in the instructions at one time; the wing lower surface stiffness depends on the panels being in place when the aircraft is on jacks.
sections.procedure: 1. Defuel the tank and drain the residual fuel through the drain valves. WARNING: FUEL VAPOUR IS EXPLOSIVE AND HARMFUL. DO NOT USE ANY NON-APPROVED ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT NEAR AN OPEN TANK AND DO NOT ENTER THE TANK WITHOUT AN ATTENDANT AT THE APERTURE. 2. Bond the aircraft to earth and confirm the bonding resistance. 3. Get access under the wing in zones 593, 692 and 595. 4. Clean the panel and the surrounding surface so that no debris can fall into the tank. 5. Remove the panel fasteners in the reverse of the torque sequence and keep them in the marked tray. CAUTION: DO NOT REMOVE MORE PANELS AT ONE TIME THAN THE NUMBER IN THE INSTRUCTIONS. THE WING LOWER SURFACE STIFFNESS DEPENDS ON THE PANELS WHEN THE AIRCRAFT IS ON JACKS. 6. Break the panel free with the approved lever at the pry points only, never at the seal groove. 7. Lower the panel and put it face down on a clean protected surface. 8. Purge the tank with the approved ventilation equipment and monitor the atmosphere continuously. 9. Confirm that the readings are inside the entry limits before any person enters. 10. Remove the seal or the sealant bead and record which closure standard was fitted. 11. Do a detailed visual inspection of the seal land or the groove and record any pitting, scoring or previous rework. 12. Check the transmitter D2810138674936 and the switch BE49012-14 mounted through the panel for security and record any leakage staining. 13. Check the clamp ROD517260-78 that carries the internal harness across the panel for security.
sections.close_out: Keep the tank ventilated and the attendant in position for the whole time the tank is open. Cover the aperture when work stops. Record the closure standard, the seal land condition and any leakage staining on the maintenance record; that record decides whether the panel can be closed to the retained seal standard.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The seal groove exists post MOD-159460 only; earlier aircraft carry a wet sealed closure.

safety_precautions: Do not enter the tank without an attendant at the aperture.
Do not remove more panels at one time than the instructions allow.
